Brand Foundation

What TraceCtrl is

TraceCtrl is the Security Observability & Control platform for agentic AI — purpose-built to give enterprises complete trace of every agent action and full control through runtime protection, attack graph risk scoring, and automated red team testing.

Brand Separation

TraceCtrl operates as a distinct product brand under CloudsineAI. It has its own visual identity, colour palette, and tone — separate from CloudsineAI's corporate brand.

The relationship is expressed as "TraceCtrl by CloudsineAI" — TraceCtrl is always the primary name; CloudsineAI is the parent endorsement. Never reverse this order.

⚠

Do not use CloudsineAI's corporate colour palette (navy #002C6B, cyan #00CDFF, amber #FFBB00) on any TraceCtrl materials. TraceCtrl's palette is Red, Melon, Black, and Faded Jade — see the Colour section for full guidance.

Category Descriptor

Always pair TraceCtrl with its category descriptor on first mention in any document, deck, or communication:

TraceCtrl — Security Observability & Control for Agentic AI

After the first mention, "TraceCtrl" alone is sufficient.

Primary Tagline

Trace Every Agent.
Control Every Risk.

Primary tagline — use on hero sections, closing slides, signage, and key brand moments.

🚫

Retired tagline — do not use: "See Every Agent. Secure Every Action. Govern Every AI." This tagline was superseded in March 2026.

Brand Strategy

Positioning

TraceCtrl is built on two pillars. Everything — copy, decks, demos, pitches — traces back to these two words: Trace and Control.

Trace

Complete observability — every agent, every action, every tool call, every data access, in real time, across any cloud or framework. Full audit trail.

Powers: Real-time OTEL telemetry · Cross-cloud agent inventory · Immutable audit logs

Control

Security enforcement — TAGAAI-powered threat modelling, runtime protection, policy-driven governance, compliance attestation.

Powers: TraceCtrl Risk (attack graphs) · TraceCtrl Guard (runtime) · TraceCtrl Strike (red team) · Compliance dashboard

Product Suite

TraceCtrl (Core)The Security Observability & Control platform — asset discovery, TAGAAI, policy engine, compliance dashboard
TraceCtrl GuardRuntime protection — ShieldPrompt prompt injection defense, 4-point guardrails, data leakage prevention

Elevator Pitches

10 Seconds

TraceCtrl is the security observability and control platform for agentic AI — full trace of every agent action and full control through runtime protection, attack graph risk scoring, and automated red team testing.

30 Seconds

Enterprises are deploying autonomous AI agents on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud — but 79% have no visibility into what those agents are actually doing. TraceCtrl is platform and framework agnostic: Trace gives you complete visibility — every agent action, every tool call, every data access, in real time. Ctrl gives you the enforcement: TraceCtrl Guard protects at runtime, TraceCtrl Risk maps attack surfaces using our Threat Attack Graph for Agentic AI (TAGAAI), and TraceCtrl Strike red-teams your agents before adversaries do — backed by our LLM Vulnerability Database.

Logo System

Logo System

The TraceCtrl logo combines the brand mark — an agent graph with a pulsing monitor node — with the wordmark "tracectrl", where "trace" is set in regular weight and "ctrl" in bold, reflecting the two halves of the product.

Logo Variants

Use the correct variant for each background. Never place a light logo on a light background or vice versa.

Primary — Light Background
Primary — Dark Background
Co-brand — "by CloudsineAI"
Brand Mark Only

When to Use Each Variant

Full Wordmark

Use in all standard contexts — website header, presentations, documents, email signatures, social media profiles, and marketing materials where there is sufficient space.

Brand Mark Only

Use only where the TraceCtrl brand is already established in context — favicons, app icons, social media profile pictures, and small format placements where the wordmark becomes illegible.

Co-brand "by CloudsineAI"

Use in external-facing contexts where the CloudsineAI parent brand needs to be visible — partner decks, investor materials, government submissions, trade show signage, and press coverage.

Light vs Dark Version

The light version (black wordmark) is for white and light grey backgrounds only. The dark version (white wordmark) is for dark backgrounds. Never place either on a red, coloured, or busy background.

Clear Space

Always maintain minimum clear space around the logo equal to the height of the brand mark — defined as x. No text, imagery, or other graphic elements should appear within this zone.

x
x
x
x

Exclusion zone (gray) = x on all four sides

= x

x = logo height

Minimum Size

Digital — 24px height minimum

Below this size the wordmark becomes illegible. Use the brand mark alone for smaller sizes.

Print — 15mm height minimum

For printed materials, the logo must be at least 15mm tall to maintain legibility at standard viewing distances.

Logo Don'ts

These misuses damage brand consistency and must be avoided in all materials.

Don't

Stretch or distort the logo in any dimension.

Don't

Place on a coloured or gradient background. Light or dark solid only.

Don't

Recolour the logo. Only approved variants are permitted.

Don't

Use at reduced opacity or as a watermark.

Don't

Apply drop shadows, glows, or visual effects.

Don't

Use the dark/white version on a light background.

Colour Palette

Colour Palette

TraceCtrl's palette is led by pure red and near-black, with Melon as a soft accent and Faded Jade as a secondary accent. Deliberately precise — communicating the seriousness of security without the approachability of consumer tech.

Semantic Risk Colours

Used exclusively in product UI, TAGAAI visualisations, and risk dashboards. Do not use these as brand accent colours in marketing materials.

Critical#FF4D4DCritical risk level
High#FF6B35High risk level
Medium#FFBB00Medium risk level
Low / Safe#22C55ELow risk / healthy state

Colour Usage Principles

60 — 30 — 10

60% near-black backgrounds. 30% white/grey text and surfaces. 10% signal red for accents, CTAs, and key moments. Never let red dominate a layout.

Red = Action or Alert

Use red for primary CTAs, the brand mark, key tagline words, section labels, and genuine alert states. Avoid decorative red — its power comes from restraint.

Contrast First

All text must meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 minimum). Off-white #F5F5F5 on Black #040404 achieves 19.6:1. Never use grey-on-grey combinations. Note: Melon (#FCBEBE) is a light accent — use on dark backgrounds only with sufficient contrast.

Type Rules

Headings

Always left-aligned. Negative letter-spacing (−0.02em) at large sizes. Never centre-align body headings — only hero/cover titles.

Weight Contrast

Use bold (700–800) for headlines. Regular (400) for body. Avoid medium (500) for large display text — it reads as undecided.

Mono Usage

Reserve JetBrains Mono for technical content only — trace IDs, API endpoints, code, and TAGAAI data. Never use it for marketing copy.

Brand Personality

Personality

TraceCtrl is the expert in the room who doesn't need to raise their voice. Authoritative, technically precise, and direct — without being cold or inaccessible.

Authoritative

We speak from 12 years of security experience. Our claims are backed by data (MIT studies, TAGAAI research, LVD records). We don't hedge or overclaim — we state.

Technically Precise

We use the correct technical language: OTEL telemetry, attack graphs, taint tracing, runtime guardrails. We don't dumb it down for security audiences. We earn trust by being precise.

Developer-Native

"Trace" and "ctrl" are words developers already own. We speak their language — OTEL-native, API-first, zero agent code changes. Security is presented as a capability, not a constraint.

Uncompromising

We don't soften the threat picture to make a sale easier. Agentic AI is a genuine attack surface. Our brand reflects the seriousness of what we protect — without fear-mongering.

Expression

Voice & Tone

How we sound is as much a trust signal as what we say. Security buyers have seen too many vendor decks. They can smell hype before the second sentence. Our voice is how we signal we're different.

01  Precise, not corporate

We say exactly what we mean. Every word earns its place. If a sentence could appear in a SOC 2 report, a McKinsey deck, or a press release from any other security vendor — rewrite it. We're not vague, we're not padded, and we don't use complexity as a substitute for clarity.

→

In practice: Short sentences. Active voice. Specific claims over general ones. "Detects lateral movement across agent chains" beats "comprehensive AI security coverage" every time.

02  Warm & direct

We're approachable without being casual, and direct without being cold. Security is a high-stakes world — our tone should make people feel like they're working with a team that gets it, not a vendor trying to impress them. Warm doesn't mean soft. Direct means we get to the point first, then back it up.

✓ This

"Agent behaviour has always been hard to trace. We built TraceCtrl to change that."

✕ Not this

"Leveraging cutting-edge observability capabilities, TraceCtrl empowers security teams to unlock unprecedented visibility into their agentic AI environments."

03  Human first, technical always

We write for people who are very good at their jobs and slightly tired of being marketed at. The test: could a sharp CISO and a senior security engineer both read this and feel like it was written for them? If the engineer finds it dumbed-down, or the CISO gets lost in the weeds — rewrite it.

→

We use real technical terms (OTEL, telemetry, attack graph, trace) without defining them every time. We explain business implications without patronising the reader about how security works.

Tone in One Sentence

Write like a trusted colleague who knows their stuff and actually wants to help — warm, direct, no fluff, no performance.

Writing Rules

✓ Always

  • Lead with the problem — the 79% visibility gap, the breach, the blind spot
  • Pair technical depth with business outcomes
  • Use developer-native language (trace, telemetry, OTEL, attack graph)
  • Name the two pillars: Trace + Control. Always.
  • Reference TAGAAI and LVD as differentiators — spell out on first use
  • Tie to enterprise proof: 12 years security DNA, 8 countries, government trust
  • Use contractions: "We don't" over "We do not"
  • Use specific numbers and named sources
  • Never fear-monger — we sell by being right, not by scaring

✕ Avoid

  • Generic "AI security" — TraceCtrl is specifically for agentic AI
  • Three-pillar See / Secure / Govern framing (retired)
  • "AI guardrails" — that's a different category
  • "ASPM" — wrong category, confuses buyers
  • TraceCtrl Discover in near-term materials — deferred roadmap
  • Sub-product names without "TraceCtrl" prefix
  • "World-class", "cutting-edge", "next-generation"
  • "Robust", "holistic", "seamless", "empower"

Tone by Audience

AudienceToneExample opener
CISOExecutive, outcome-focused. Lead with governance and board readiness."79% of enterprises have no visibility into what their AI agents are actually doing."
Cloud ArchitectTechnical, peer-to-peer. Skip the preamble, go straight to capability."OTEL-native, multi-cloud, API-first. Think CSPM for agentic AI."

Expression

Words in Practice

The quick reference for anyone writing under time pressure. Swap these phrases, retire these words.

Swap These Out

Instead of…Say…
"Revolutionising security observability""Finally, traces that tell you what actually happened"
"AI-powered threat intelligence""We use ML where it helps. We tell you when it doesn't."
"Seamless, frictionless experience""It works. And when it doesn't, you'll know why."
"Empowering security teams""Less guessing. More fixing."
"Next-gen" / "game-changer"Describe what specifically changed — with evidence
"Robust" / "holistic"Specific: reliable, end-to-end, tested

Retire These Entirely

Never sayBecauseSay instead
RobustMeans nothingReliable, proven, tested
HolisticConsultant-speakComplete, end-to-end
SeamlessNo product is seamlessSimple, straightforward
EmpowerHollowHelp, enable, let
Proactive postureSecurity theater languageDescribe the actual capability
Game-changerEvery vendor says thisDescribe the concrete change

Quick Reference Card

→ Lead with the problem. 79% of enterprises lack visibility into their AI agents. Open with the gap.
→ Name the pillars. Trace + Control. Always. Every significant piece.
→ Use contractions. "We don't" over "We do not." We're not writing a legal brief.
→ Write short sentences. Two clauses maximum. Then break.
→ Earn the joke. Dry wit works when grounded. A sharp observation beats a forced pun.
→ No stats without sources. If we cite it, we can prove it. If we can't, we don't.
→ Never fear-monger. We sell by being right. Not by scaring.
